# Model Output and Measurement Checklist: A quiz on a chapter or a book

**Purpose**: Test whether the requirements on the model's replies, the key check and the
measurement are complete, clear, consistent and measurable. These are the riskiest parts of the
feature: a new prompt, a new reader of model output, and a check that acts as a judge
(constitution V, VI).
**Created**: 2026-11-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), with [plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md) and
[contracts/](../contracts/)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Resolution, 2026-11-10**: at the owner's request ("resolve the checklist"), every item was
settled by a change to the spec, plan, research, data model or contracts. Each is marked with what
resolved it. Four rest on a default the agent chose, marked **[owner to confirm]**: CHK014,
CHK021, CHK030 and CHK032. Uncheck any whose resolution you don't accept.

## The writer's replies: completeness

- [x] CHK001 Does the spec require the explanation to be stated by the passage, as FR-005 requires
  of the key? In the probe, Q16's explanation invented the reason its passage didn't give.
  [Gap, Spec §FR-004, §FR-005]
  → FR-004 now requires it. FR-020's rubric marks "an explanation beyond the passage" as a flaw.
- [x] CHK002 Is a functional requirement behind SC-002's length target? Only the contract asks
  for wrong answers "of about the same length and form". [Gap, Spec §SC-002,
  contracts/model-replies.md]
  → FR-004 now requires the four wrong options to match the right one's length and form, tied to
  SC-002.
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements defined for a reply written in a language other than the one named?
  Is it refused and written again, accepted, or counted? [Gap, Spec §FR-003, §FR-010]
  → FR-010 adds the refusal kind `wrong_language`, for a confident identification only. Research R4
  and the reply contract use the existing `reply_language`.
- [x] CHK004 Does the spec say whether a question may ask the reader to infer from the passage
  ("arguments, explanations"), or only to recall what it states? The two readings of FR-005 lead
  to different marks. [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005]
  → FR-005 now allows following the passage's reasoning when the passage states the answer, or
  the steps to it. No outside inference or knowledge is allowed.
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements defined for a passage in one language and questions in another? Is
  "stated by its passage" judged across languages, by the writer and by the checker?
  [Coverage, Spec §FR-003, §FR-005, §FR-024]
  → FR-005 now judges it by meaning, across the two languages.

## The writer's replies: clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "nothing to ask about" defined for borderline passages, such as a table of real
  data, an epigraph, a chapter's own summary or a figure caption with figures? Or is FR-007's list
  meant to be exhaustive? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, Edge Cases]
  → FR-007 now defines it by what a passage does: it only points elsewhere or names things. It
  says which borderline cases are asked about: tables of figures, events, epigraphs, summaries, and
  captions that state something.
- [x] CHK007 Is FR-009's list of forbidden options ("such as …") exhaustive, or illustrative? Is
  the rule stated generally enough that a reader of a reply could apply it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
  → FR-009 is now a general rule: every option readable on its own. The examples are only
  illustrative. Detection is best effort, and the reading marks what gets through.
- [x] CHK008 Is "repeated options" defined: identical text only, or also options that say the same
  thing in other words? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
  → FR-010 defines it as the same text, ignoring case, spacing and final punctuation. Paraphrases
  are left to the reading, as two defensible options.

## Reading and refusing replies

- [x] CHK009 FR-010 lists "a passage other than the one given" as a form failure. Is that still
  meaningful now that the writer names no passage (research R3)? [Conflict, Spec §FR-010,
  research.md R3]
  → Removed from FR-010.
- [x] CHK010 Does the spec define what happens when every passage of a chosen chapter is skipped?
  For example, a one-chapter quiz on *Referências bibliográficas*. The rule ruling out a chapter
  after two skips is in the plan only. [Gap, Spec §FR-007, §FR-010, research.md R5]
  → FR-007 now holds the rule: two skipped passages in a row. A whole-book quiz moves the
  questions to other chapters; a one-chapter quiz ends, saying the chapter has nothing to ask
  about.
- [x] CHK011 Are the kinds of refusal the measurement reports defined in the spec, or only in the
  data model? FR-019 asks for "the replies it couldn't read, by kind". [Traceability, Spec
  §FR-019, data-model.md § Draft]
  → FR-010 now lists the kinds, and FR-019 reports by them, with skips, passed-over passages and
  unreadable verdicts.
- [x] CHK012 Is the decision to accept two questions on the same point a documented assumption
  with a reason, or an untested gap? [Assumption, Spec Edge Cases]
  → The edge case now gives the reason: a weaker quiz, not a wrong one, and a model call per pair
  to check.

## The key check: requirement completeness

- [x] CHK013 Is the check's behavior on a verdict it can't read in the spec? Research R11 shows
  the question; FR-012 says questions appear "after any check". [Gap, Spec §FR-012, §FR-024,
  research.md R11]
  → FR-024 now says: asked twice, then the question is shown, logged and counted.
- [x] CHK014 FR-027 depends on "the time the plan allots", but the plan's Order of work gives no
  time. Is the time box defined somewhere? [Gap, Conflict, Spec §FR-027, plan.md]
  → The bound is attempts, not time: at most three wordings, each with the writer and at most one
  other model (FR-027, plan step 6). **[owner to confirm]**
- [x] CHK015 Is "the generating model's own open-book answer" defined when known cases were
  written by different models: the probe's gpt-oss, and later others? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-027]
  → FR-027 now defines the comparator as the shipped writer model answering each case, whoever
  wrote it.
- [x] CHK016 Is "the remaining rate of flawed keys" defined: measured on which questions, with
  the check on or off, and recorded where? [Clarity, Spec §FR-027]
  → FR-027 now defines it: the share of flawed keys in the marked reading of a run in the shipped
  configuration (SC-003). It is recorded in `docs/benchmark-results.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.
- [x] CHK017 Do the requirements guard against fitting the check to its own test? Several
  wordings and models are tried on the same known cases that decide the rule. Is part of the
  cases held out, or the selection otherwise accounted for? [Gap, Spec §FR-026, §FR-027]
  → FR-026 now splits development cases, for trying wordings, from test cases, marked afterwards
  from runs no wording saw. FR-027's rule runs once, on the test cases. See also research R11 and
  `contracts/quiz-experiments.md` (`case_set`).

## The key check: measurability

- [x] CHK018 With 10 flawed and 30 sound cases, one case moves a share by 10 or 3 points. Do
  FR-027's conditions state how uncertainty is read? Constitution VI counts a difference only when
  its interval excludes zero. [Measurability, Consistency, Spec §FR-027, Constitution VI]
  → Condition (a) is now a paired difference whose bootstrap interval (4,000 resamples, 95%) must
  exclude zero. Condition (b) stays a threshold on a share, reported with its counts.
- [x] CHK019 Is "rejects a larger share" in FR-027 (a) defined for a tie, and is a tie a failure?
  [Clarity, Spec §FR-027]
  → FR-027 now says a tie fails, which the interval rule implies anyway.
- [x] CHK020 Is the labeling rubric for known cases documented, with what makes a key "sound" or
  "flawed"? The probe's four flaw kinds (wrong, unsupported, two defensible, flawed stem) aren't
  defined in the spec. [Gap, Spec §FR-026, §SC-003]
  → FR-020 now holds the rubric, with six flaw reasons. A weak wording on a sound key counts as
  sound with a note, as the probe counted Q2, Q7, Q9 and Q13.
- [x] CHK021 Is it stated who labels known cases and marks readings, and whether the owner
  reviews labels made by the agent? [Assumption, Spec §FR-020, §FR-026]
  → Assumptions: the implementing agent marks, and the owner reviews every flawed label and a
  sample of the sound ones before FR-027's rule. **[owner to confirm]**

## The measurement: completeness and clarity

- [x] CHK022 Is "repeatable" in FR-019 defined: the same passages, or the same questions too? At
  temperature 0.2, even a fixed seed may not repeat the questions. [Clarity, Spec §FR-019,
  research.md R6]
  → FR-019 now defines it: the same passages, order and letters for the same seed. The questions
  may differ.
- [x] CHK023 Are the measurement's exact chapters and numbers of questions recorded where the spec
  can be checked? The spec names the books; research R12 names the chapters.
  [Traceability, Spec §FR-019, research.md R12]
  → FR-019 now names all six chapters, with counts or FR-002's default.
- [x] CHK024 Is "where in each chapter the questions come from" given a measurable form, such as
  the share in each third? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019, §SC-005]
  → FR-019 now reports "the share of each chapter's questions in each third of the chapter".
- [x] CHK025 Is the "answerable without the passages" measure deliberately left without a target?
  `problem.md` left it open pending FR-005's scope, which is now settled. [Gap, Consistency, Spec
  §FR-019, Success Criteria]
  → Yes, deliberately: FR-019 says it has no target, and why. A subject can be known without the
  book.
- [x] CHK026 Is it stated whether the measurement runs with the key check on or off, and whether
  SC-003 is judged in the configuration that ships? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-003, §FR-027]
  → FR-019 now says SC-002 to SC-004 are judged on a run in the configuration that ships.
- [x] CHK027 Is a requirement in the spec that no passage of a book that isn't public enters the
  repository, through known cases, readings or results? It is only in research R12 and the
  contracts. [Gap, Spec §FR-020, §FR-026]
  → FR-020 and FR-026 now require it.
- [x] CHK028 Are unmarked or partly marked readings covered? Constitution VI asks that what can't
  be scored be left out and counted, never scored as zero. [Coverage, Spec §FR-020, Constitution
  VI]
  → FR-020 now counts the marked questions only, reports the unmarked ones, and never counts them
  either way.

## Acceptance criteria quality

- [x] CHK029 Does SC-003 state how many questions must be read by hand for its 90% to mean
  something: all of a run, or a minimum sample? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
  → SC-003 now reads every question of the run, about 85.
- [x] CHK030 Are SC-002's 35% and SC-004's 95% justified by a reason or a measurement, or are they
  open assumptions to revisit? [Assumption, Spec §SC-002, §SC-004]
  → Each now states its reason. They remain targets this spec sets, not measured limits.
  **[owner to confirm]**
- [x] CHK031 Do SC-001 to SC-006 say whether one measurement run settles them, or whether several
  seeds or runs are needed? [Measurability, Spec Success Criteria, Constitution VI]
  → The Success Criteria now open with how each is judged: by construction, on one full run in the
  shipped configuration, on the quickstart's quiz, or by the owner.
- [x] CHK032 Can SC-013, the qualitative one, be checked by anyone but the owner, and is it meant
  to block delivery? [Measurability, Spec §SC-013]
  → SC-013 is now the owner's report after use, and not a gate. **[owner to confirm]**

## Consistency across the documents

- [x] CHK033 Do the spec's FR-012 ("after any check"), the contract's acceptance of an unreadable
  verdict, and research R11 describe the same flow? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, contracts/model-replies.md]
  → They do now, through FR-024's unreadable-verdict rule.
- [x] CHK034 Are the record requirements consistent? FR-031 names `README.md` and
  `docs/decisions.md`. Constitution VIII and the plan also name `docs/benchmark-results.md` for the
  runs. [Consistency, Spec §FR-031, Constitution VIII]
  → FR-031 now names `docs/benchmark-results.md`.
- [x] CHK035 Is the check's reasoning setting a requirement? It appears in the plan and data model
  only. The summary judge failed at `low`, so does the spec need it to prove itself at the
  setting that ships? [Gap, Spec §FR-025, research.md R11]
  → FR-025 now makes it a setting, and FR-027's rule is applied at the level that ships.
- [x] CHK036 Do FR-019's list of reported measures and contracts/quiz-experiments.md's report
  sections name the same measures? [Consistency, Spec §FR-019, contracts/quiz-experiments.md]
  → The contract's report list now matches FR-019 one for one.

## Dependencies and assumptions

- [x] CHK037 Is the measurement's dependency on the benchmarks restored from `c7bb785`, and on the
  owner's copy of the book, stated as an assumption with what happens when either is missing?
  [Dependency, Spec Assumptions, quickstart.md § 7]
  → The Assumptions now say a run stops before any work, naming what is missing or differs.
- [x] CHK038 Is the assumption that a 500-token passage always fits documented with what happens
  if chunking settings change? [Assumption, Spec §FR-011, research.md R2]
  → FR-011 now says a passage that doesn't fit is passed over and counted, and that the rule holds
  if chunking or the window change.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
- Scope: the writer's replies, the key check and the measurement, at the owner's request. The
  Quiz tab's layout and the download are left to the spec's own checklist and to `/speckit-analyze`.
